purpose: Price the custom cisTarget database required by amendment 1, from MEASURED runs rather than an estimate, so the decision to build it (or not) rests on numbers.

configuration.storage: Windows bind mount (D: drive) presented to the container as /data

measurements.note: These are the tool's OWN reported timings for the Cluster-Buster scoring phase, which isolates motif scanning from database writing. They are preferred over the wrapper's wall-clock because the wrapper's timer also includes feather I/O.

run_24_motifs.concurrent_load: none of this lane's other jobs

run_120_motifs.why_wrapper_time_unmeasured: The wrapper's own timing echo was lost to the shell defect recorded as self-audit S16. The database itself completed correctly and all feathers were written; only the wrapper's trailing echo was lost.
run_120_motifs.concurrent_load: A full-file scan of the 63.6 GB fragment file was running on the same machine for part of this run. This is a known confound that inflates the measured per-motif cost.

two_point_analysis.interpretation_HONEST: The implied intercept is NEGATIVE, which means a simple linear fixed-plus-marginal model does not describe these two points. A negative fixed cost is not physical. The most likely causes are (a) thread-scheduling granularity -- 24 motifs is roughly 1.5 waves of 16 threads while 120 is 7.5 waves -- and (b) the I/O contention during the 120-motif run. No fitted model is reported, because a two-point fit that produces an unphysical intercept should not be dressed up as a projection.

projection_for_the_full_collection.method: Simple per-motif scaling from each measured point separately, reported as a RANGE rather than a single fitted number.
projection_for_the_full_collection.both_routes_hours: 67 to 83, since amendment 1 requires a custom database over each route's own region universe
projection_for_the_full_collection.confidence_statement: This is a projection from two measured points, not a measurement of the full build. It is labelled as such and must not be cited as a measured runtime.

separate_io_concern_that_may_dominate.observation: Writing the regions-vs-motifs scores feather took 162 s and the rankings feather 146 s at only 24 motifs, for files of roughly 45 MB each, over the Windows bind mount.
separate_io_concern_that_may_dominate.extrapolated_artifact_size: At 10,249 motifs the regions-vs-motifs scores matrix is 150,561 x 10,249 float32, which is approximately 6.2 GB, and the rankings database is of comparable size.
separate_io_concern_that_may_dominate.risk: Feather write time over a bind mount may become a large or dominant share of total runtime, and is NOT included in the scoring-phase projection above.
separate_io_concern_that_may_dominate.recommendation: Build to container-local or WSL-native storage and copy the finished databases to the output directory afterwards. This is an engineering change only; it alters no scientific parameter.

decision_surfaced_not_taken.fact: Amendment 1 requires a custom cisTarget database per route. The measured price is roughly 34 to 41 hours of 16-thread compute per route, plus unmeasured feather I/O.
decision_surfaced_not_taken.this_lane_does_not_unilaterally_change_t: The amendment's scientific reasoning is unaffected by its cost: using one custom and one generic database would confound region universe with database type and would defeat the only question Route B exists to answer.
options_for_the_owner: Accept the compute cost and run both builds (recommended, and the only option that preserves the isolation).
Run on more cores; the scoring phase is embarrassingly parallel across motifs.

Reduce the motif collection -- but note this would have to be a PROSPECTIVE, documented restriction applied identically to both routes, and it directly weakens control C1, whose whole point is that annotation supply varies 144-fold across TFs.
decision_surfaced_not_taken.what_must_not_happen: Silently reducing the motif collection, or quietly reverting to a generic database for one route, because the full build proved expensive.

artifacts_produced.note: Benchmark databases only. These are NOT usable as real cisTarget databases and are written under a BENCHMARK_ prefix so they cannot be mistaken for one.

region_fasta.reconciliation: sequence count equals BED region count exactly; the builder stops if it does not

artifacts_produced.motif_list_digest_caveat: The motif-list digests recorded for these two benchmark runs are NOT reliable, because at the time they ran the builder wrote the list to a shared fixed path that the second run overwrote. See self-audit S12. The TIMING measurements are unaffected, since they do not depend on that file. The defect is fixed for all future runs.

what_this_receipt_does_not_claim: That a full custom cisTarget database exists. It does not.
That the projected runtime has been observed. It has not.
That the benchmark databases are usable for motif enrichment. They are not.
